acceptance_note: NO CLOSE. Neither Question1 nor Question2 (nor either negation) is proved. Every theorem below is either an unconditional lemma or a CONDITIONAL whose extra hypothesis is visible in its own statement. Nothing here asserts an answer to Erdos 1191.
verbatim_check: 8/8 byte-identical (line-block diff against the frozen spec)

sealed.name: Erdos1191.sidon_intSub_inj
sealed.what: Sidon (sum form, as the spec fixes it) => all differences distinct, stated over Z so no Nat-subtraction truncation can hide a case.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.sidon_offDiag_bound
sealed.what: k*k - k <= 2*floor(x): the k(k-1) ordered pairs of distinct elements of A cap [1,x] inject into the 2*floor(x) nonzero integers of absolute value <= floor(x).

sealed.name: Erdos1191.sidon_card_sq_le
sealed.what: Subtraction-free form: k^2 <= k + 2*floor(x).

sealed.name: Erdos1191.countUpTo_le_sqrt
sealed.what: The classical counting bound in real form: |A cap [1,x]| <= sqrt(2x) + 1 for every Sidon A.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.sidonWeight_le
sealed.what: sidonWeight A c x <= (sqrt 2 + 1) * (log x)^c for x >= 1, uniformly over ALL Sidon sets.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.sidonWeight_mono_exponent
sealed.what: For x >= e the weight is monotone increasing in the exponent c.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.eventually_le_half_of_eventually_le
sealed.what: THE UPGRADE. An eventual positive lower bound at ANY exponent c <= 1/2 is automatically one at c = 1/2. Junk-free: a statement about the weight, not about liminf.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.bddAbove_liminfSet_iff
sealed.what: THE JUNK GATE, characterised: BddAbove of the eventual-lower-bound set <-> NOT Tendsto f atTop atTop. The spec header names this trap; this makes it a theorem.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.le_liminf_of_eventually_le_of_not_tendsto
sealed.what: With the gate discharged, an eventual lower bound really is a liminf lower bound.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.not_question1_of_witness
sealed.what: CONDITIONAL. A Question2'-style witness at any exponent c <= 1/2, PLUS the gate at 1/2, refutes Question1. The gate hypothesis is displayed, not hidden.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.question2_of_witness
sealed.what: CONDITIONAL. The junk-free Question2' witness upgrades to the liminf form Question2, given the gate at its own exponent.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.sidonWeight_zero_le
sealed.what: sidonWeight A 0 x <= sqrt 2 + 1 for x >= 1: at exponent 0 the weight is BOUNDED.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.not_tendsto_sidonWeight_zero
sealed.what: THE GATE, DISCHARGED UNCONDITIONALLY AT EXPONENT 0, for every Sidon set.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.liminf_sidonWeight_zero_le_const
sealed.what: THE EXPONENT-0 CASE OF THE ERDOS BOUND, PROVED. Same shape as the spec's sorried erdos_liminf_sqrt_log_le_const with 1/2 replaced by 0, no sorry. Localises the whole difficulty of that theorem in the (log x)^(1/2) factor.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.liminf_eq_zero_of_tendsto_atTop
sealed.what: If the weight blows up, Mathlib's liminf returns Real.sSup's junk value 0.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.question1_clause_holds_vacuously
sealed.what: FIDELITY FINDING 1. On any set whose weight tends to +infinity - where the mathematician's liminf is +infinity, maximally FAR from 0 - the formalised Question1 clause holds anyway, for the junk reason.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.erdos_bound_vacuous_on_blowup
sealed.what: FIDELITY FINDING 2. The same junk makes the spec's sorried Erdos bound hold trivially for EVERY nonnegative constant on exactly those sets.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.question1_iff_restricted
sealed.what: THE REDUCTION. Question1 <-> its own restriction to the non-blowup case. Any attack may assume the gate for free, and gains nothing from blowup sets.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.not_liminf_pos_of_blowup
sealed.what: THE ASYMMETRY, made precise. A blowup set can never witness Question2 (its formalised liminf is 0) yet can satisfy every Question2' clause. The two readings are NOT interchangeable.

sealed.name: Erdos1191.finite_countSet
sealed.axioms: re-proved verbatim from the spec as a control; not printed separately
sealed.what: Spec control, copied so the file is self-contained.

open.item: Question1 (a named target) - UNTOUCHED as a whole
open.obstruction: Reduced by question1_iff_restricted to the non-blowup case. In that case the statement is the genuine open problem: liminf A(x)(log x)^(1/2)/sqrt(x) = 0 for every infinite Sidon A.

open.item: Question2 / Question2' (a named target) - UNTOUCHED as a whole
open.obstruction: No infinite Sidon set is CONSTRUCTED anywhere in this artifact, and none exists in the spec either (the spec's only Sidon witness is a singleton). Both question2_of_witness and not_question1_of_witness are therefore currently un-instantiable: they consume a witness nobody has built. Building a Lean infinite Sidon set (e.g. the Mian-Chowla greedy set, or Ruzsa/Erdos-Turan style constructions) is the prerequisite, and is itself a substantial independent formalization.

open.item: The gate at exponent 1/2: NOT Tendsto (sidonWeight A (1/2)) atTop atTop
open.obstruction: THE ONE LOAD-BEARING GAP. Discharged unconditionally at exponent 0 (not_tendsto_sidonWeight_zero) via the trivial counting bound k <= sqrt(2x)+1. That bound gives sidonWeight A c x <= (sqrt 2 + 1)(log x)^c, which is BOUNDED only for c <= 0 and unbounded for every c > 0. So the elementary counting argument cannot reach c = 1/2 at all. The gate at c = 1/2 is exactly the qualitative content of the published Erdos bound (liminf finite), whose proof is the dyadic-scale / convexity-over-blocks argument: split [1,x] into blocks of length y, apply convexity to the block counts, sum the resulting distinct-difference budget over dyadic scales x, x/2, x/4, ... The single-scale version of that argument reproves only the trivial sqrt(2x) bound - the log factor is produced by the sum over scales. Formalizing it needs a Finset convexity/Cauchy-Schwarz step plus a dyadic sum with uniform error control; well beyond an 8-iteration budget.

open.item: The c > 1/2 direction of the exponent comparison
open.obstruction: sidonWeight_mono_exponent runs the wrong way for c > 1/2: weight(1/2) = weight(c) * (log x)^(1/2 - c) -> 0. So a Question2 witness at c > 1/2 is CONSISTENT with Question1 and yields no contradiction. Only c <= 1/2 witnesses bear on Question1, which is what not_question1_of_witness records.

fidelity_flag_for_the_semantic_court: Three of the sealed theorems (question1_clause_holds_vacuously, erdos_bound_vacuous_on_blowup, not_liminf_pos_of_blowup) are machine-checked evidence bearing on the row's own claimCeiling sentence 'It does NOT assert the formalization is faithful.' They show the Mathlib-liminf rendering of Question1 is satisfied, for junk reasons, on exactly the sets where the intended mathematical statement would be most false, and that Question2 and Question2' come apart there. This is a report about the FORMALIZATION, not about Erdos 1191.
